items.title: US reportedly pursuing a Russia–Ukraine peace agreement
items.summary: BRICS News reports that Washington says it is working toward an agreement acceptable to both Moscow and Kyiv. The post offers no details of proposed terms or a negotiation timetable.

items.title: Putin and Xi expected to discuss Ukraine in China
items.summary: DD Geopolitics cites Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov as saying Putin and Xi Jinping will meet on November 18 during Putin's planned China visit, with Ukraine among the foreign-policy topics.

items.title: Report suggests Trump and Putin may discuss Ukraine in China
items.summary: BRICS News claims the US and Russian presidents are expected to discuss Ukraine during talks in China. The post does not establish a confirmed meeting schedule.

items.title: Crimean Bridge reportedly struck; road traffic disrupted
items.summary: DD Geopolitics reports that Crimean official Sergei Aksyonov announced a temporary bridge closure after a Ukrainian attack. The channel separately describes satellite imagery that it says suggests damage; the extent remains unverified.

items.title: Russia seeking positions at UN telecommunications agency
items.summary: DD Geopolitics reports that Russia is contesting seats on the International Telecommunication Union's Council and Radio Regulations Board, citing diplomatic assessments of its prospects. Election outcomes were not established in the post.

items.title: Germany calls for wider EU burden-sharing on Ukraine aid
items.summary: According to DD Geopolitics, German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul urged European partners to distribute support for Ukraine's energy and air-defense needs more evenly during the coming winter.

items.title: Cargo vessel carrying Ukrainian wheat sinks in Black Sea
items.summary: DD Geopolitics reports that the BETUL 8 sank off Bulgaria while transporting Ukrainian wheat, with all 12 crew rescued. The channel says investigators are examining whether an explosion involved a mine or drone; the cause is not established.

items.title: Report describes proposed €45 billion EU loan to Ukraine
items.summary: DD Geopolitics says the European Commission is preparing a proposed €45 billion loan to help cover Ukraine's anticipated 2027 financing gap. The report describes the proposal as requiring unanimous approval; no adoption is confirmed.

items.title: Russian air attacks reportedly targeted Ukrainian military sites
items.summary: DD Geopolitics claims Russian bombs hit a temporary base of Ukraine's 128th Mountain Assault Brigade near Zarechnoye and a rocket hit a drone-launch site. Damage and casualties were not independently established.

items.title: French personnel reportedly operating in Ukraine on training mission
items.summary: DD Geopolitics and Intel Slava repeat an investigation attributed to RFI alleging small French military teams have entered Ukraine to train personnel and maintain supplied weapons. The posts say Paris has not officially confirmed the mission.

items.title: Locomotives reportedly targeted across three Ukrainian regions
items.summary: Intel Slava claims Russian Geran drones hit locomotives near Serbka in Odesa region, Matviivka in Zaporizhzhia region, and Dnipro. The number destroyed and operational impact are not independently verified.

items.title: Ukraine reportedly warned of potential Russian energy strikes
items.summary: Intel Slava attributes to Ukrainian Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat reports of warnings about preparations for another Russian attack on energy and critical infrastructure. This concerns a possible future strike, not a confirmed attack.

items.title: Russia claims 290,000 Ukrainian drones downed since invasion
items.summary: Intel Slava relays a cumulative Russian Defence Ministry claim of 290,000 drones shot down. The channel itself notes uncertainty over the counting method; the figure has not been independently verified.

items.title: EU reportedly expands Russia-related sanctions listings
items.summary: DD Geopolitics reports that the EU listed Irish RT correspondent Chay Bowes among 30 individuals and two entities under measures concerning information interference and cyber activity. The listing details require official confirmation.

items.title: Estonia reportedly preparing continuity-of-government plans
items.summary: DD Geopolitics cites Politico reporting on Estonia's preparations to operate digital government services from abroad if its territory were occupied, building on data backups in Luxembourg. The scenario is contingency planning, not an announced evacuation.

items.title: Edible-oil processing facility reportedly hit in Dnipro
items.summary: DD Geopolitics cites local media reporting an attack on a major vegetable-oil facility associated with the Oleyna brand in Dnipro. The channel provides no independently verified damage assessment.

items.title: Munich Security Conference chair raises Crimea in negotiations
items.summary: DD Geopolitics quotes Wolfgang Ischinger arguing that any discussion of restoring earlier European security arrangements should also address Crimea's return to Ukraine and Russian withdrawal from eastern Ukraine.

items.title: Italian political figure reportedly conditions support on ending Ukraine aid
items.summary: DD Geopolitics cites Politico as reporting that Roberto Vannacci wants Italian military assistance to Ukraine ended as a condition for supporting Giorgia Meloni's government. This is a reported political demand, not an enacted policy.

items.title: EU foreign-policy chief seeks role in Russia negotiations
items.summary: DD Geopolitics reports that EU foreign-policy chief Kaja Kallas wants EU expertise reflected in negotiations with Russia, despite resistance to her direct participation. The report does not confirm any change in negotiating representation.

items.title: Zaporizhzhia bridge reportedly closed following Russian strikes
items.summary: DD Geopolitics says regional authorities closed the Preobrazhensky Bridge after Russian attacks in Zaporizhzhia. A separate post describes traffic diversions; the structural condition and reopening time remain unclear.

items.title: Odesa region electricity outages reported after strikes
items.summary: DD Geopolitics cites energy company DTEK as saying Russian attacks on its facilities in Odesa region left more than 52,200 customers without power. The duration of the outages was not specified.

items.title: Estonia calls for tougher EU sanctions against Russia
items.summary: DD Geopolitics says Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna criticized resistance to further sanctions, while Brussels was preparing possible new designations targeting individuals, firms and shipping-related networks.

items.title: Russia claims 1,336 Ukrainian drones intercepted overnight
items.summary: DD Geopolitics relays a Russian Defence Ministry assertion that air defenses downed 1,336 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions. BRICS News separately describes an unusually large Ukrainian attack, but neither post independently verifies the tally.

items.title: Passenger bus reportedly hit in Zaporizhzhia region
items.summary: DD Geopolitics alleges a Ukrainian attack on a passenger bus in the Zaporizhzhia region injured its driver and two passengers. The location, circumstances and responsibility have not been independently confirmed.

items.title: UK minister says peace terms must be acceptable to Ukraine
items.summary: DD Geopolitics quotes a British defense minister saying any proposed peace agreement must be acceptable to Ukraine and rejecting Russian demands over European defense policy.

items.title: Russia claims attacks on Ukrainian shipping and rail logistics
items.summary: DD Geopolitics relays a Russian Defence Ministry statement claiming strikes on a cargo ship headed for Chornomorsk and a railway locomotive near Zaporizhzhia. The claimed military use and damage have not been independently confirmed.

items.title: Oil storage sites in Russia reportedly damaged by Ukrainian drones
items.summary: Intel Slava reports a drone hit on an oil depot in Azov and claims satellite imagery showed five tanks destroyed at Ust-Luga following a November 11 attack. These are separate reported incidents, with damage figures unverified.

items.title: Zelensky claims Ukraine disabled over half of Russian refining capacity
items.summary: Intel Slava quotes Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky as saying Ukrainian attacks had disabled more than 55% of Russia's oil-refining capacity. The extent and meaning of the reported disruption have not been independently verified.

items.title: Estonia reports attempted attack on drone manufacturer
items.summary: Intel Slava reproduces an Estonian security-service statement alleging a November 14 attempted arson or explosion at drone maker Threod Systems and the detention of suspects. The statement warns about possible Russian recruitment; attribution remains under investigation.

items.title: Drone-dropped mines reportedly injure civilians in Russia's Rylsk
items.summary: Intel Slava claims Ukrainian drones dropped mines in central Rylsk, Kursk region, severely injuring two civilians. The allegations and reported injuries have not been independently verified.
